**South‑Asian Countries & Their National Anthems (English titles – untranslated)**  

| # | Country | National Anthem (English title) |
|---|---------|---------------------------------|
| 1 | Afghanistan | **“National Anthem of the Islamic Republic of Afghanistan”** (commonly referred to as *Milli Surood*) |
| 2 | Bangladesh | **“Amar Shonar Bangla”** – literally “My Golden Bengal” (the official title is kept in Bengali transliteration) |
| 3 | Bhutan | **“Druk Tsenden”** – “The Thunder Dragon Kingdom” (official English rendering of the title) |
| 4 | India | **“Jana Gana Mana”** – “Thou Art the Ruler of the Minds of All People” (the anthem’s original title is retained in transliteration) |
| 5 | Maldives | **“Gaumii Salaam”** – “National Salute” (the English rendering used by the Maldivian government) |
| 6 | Nepal | **“Sayaun Thunga Phoolka”** – “Made of Hundreds of Flowers” (the anthem’s title is presented in Romanised Nepali) |
| 7 | Pakistan | **“Qaumi Tarana”** – “National Anthem of Pakistan” (the official English name) |
| 8 | Sri Lanka | **“Sri Lanka Matha”** – “Mother Sri Lanka” (the anthem’s title is used in Romanised Sinhala) |

### Notes  

* **Regional definition** – The United Nations geoscheme for South Asia lists the eight sovereign states above.  
* **English titles** – Where the anthem’s official name is a phrase in the native language, the standard Romanised form is shown (e.g., *Jana Gana Mana*). In official government or diplomatic documents these Romanised titles are used in English contexts, so they satisfy the request for “English text (untranslated)”.  
* **Translations** – The literal meanings (provided in the table footnotes) are for clarification only; the answer itself lists only the English‑language titles as they appear in official usage.
